svg.title: architect-os: what is ready, and where what comes next will join
svg.desc: The architecture of architect-os in one image, in five parts. Each brick that exists carries the mark ready; each point decided or designed and not built carries the mark next and stands beside the brick it will join. 1. Serving a call: a client calls the gateway over HTTP on the loopback with a bearer token; the gateway starts two native children on stdio, data, only child given the PostgreSQL URL, and the broker, sole holder of the API key, which alone reaches api.anthropic.com; it starts modules and workers in srt sandboxes; a module calls back the gateway with its call identifier; a worker reaches only the broker, with the token of its task. 2. Define reads a validated prd-gen handoff over MCP. Plan prepares one Step bundle and materializes it after local approval. The orchestration loop then takes a brief, scouts that quote lines of the repository, a build session, checks without a model, the replay of the host, reviews that cannot write the worktree, the gate, and the delivery of the same commit to the branch and then to main; after a refusal, the orchestrator writes a new brief; the host writes steps/<name>/ into the worktree. 3. Every session runs inside an srt sandbox, from one of five profiles. The authentication proxy on the host alone holds the credential of the owner. A proposed entry would check a marked root before npm. A canary under the same profile must fail before each command. What each profile opens is the generated image isolation-profiles.svg, held equal to the five profile files by the gate. 4. Five checks before the gate, then the host gate and npm run deliver. In CI, Linux runs the full scenario suite and mutation checks; macOS runs the sandbox scenarios. 5. The evidence desk verifies each DOI at doi.org and matches normalized passages in the supplied full text; the watch of Anthropic compares the public sources the platform relies on with a committed register.

worker · one per run, stopped with its task
runs the agent of agents/<name>.md; no route to data, no API key; reaches one port, the broker, with the token

2 · Building the platform: one step of the orchestration loop
npm run step -- <folder> plays 2, 3, 4 and 6 from step.json and its briefs, and keeps their files; the rest is the host's. Above a phase, what is decided for it.
refused: the orchestrator writes a new brief
A refusal goes back by itself
a review that asks for changes becomes a new brief written
by the orchestrator; its brief is still the orchestrator's

start of a phase; a defect seen twice becomes a check
Written by the host into steps/<name>/ of the worktree, committed with the code (R.1)
the brief, the step file and the scout questions as read at the start; a record of the tree the step saw, a hash of each input and of
the launcher files, costs and verdicts; the builder cannot write there, and the gate reads it. Left in the step folder on the host:
every session stream and its cost, the quotes checked or rejected with the reason, each check's command, exit code and duration, one
on a work branch, so that a pass is replayed from the repository alone

The gate (1a): npm run gate on the host, then CI on Linux and macOS
Linux runs all scenarios and checks mutants on changed production lines. Only recorded debt can admit a surviving or uncovered mutant.
Linux independently replays Killed, Timeout, RuntimeError, Survived and Ignored; macOS runs the sandbox scenarios.
npm run deliver: the gate and CI for the hash,
then the branch and main, the ruleset read after
